title: A die's device and wiring layers
caption: Metal interconnect sits above the device layer and silicon substrate in this die-oriented view. Packaging is a separate assembly around the die, not another on-chip film. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Metal wiring
nodes.detail: Multiple patterned layers route signals and power.

nodes.label: Device layer
nodes.detail: Gates control current near the silicon surface.

nodes.label: Silicon foundation
nodes.detail: A single crystal supports the devices.

title: Follow the changing physical object
caption: Each stage passes a different object to the next specialist; value and elapsed time accumulate along that path. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Purified crystal
nodes.detail: Quartz becomes polysilicon, then a single crystal.

nodes.label: Patterned wafer
nodes.detail: Fab processes repeat across many die sites.

nodes.label: Connected assembly
nodes.detail: Tested dies join memory and package wiring.

nodes.label: Computing system
nodes.detail: Boards, cooling and networking make the chip useful.

title: Three streams meet in the package
caption: Logic, memory and package interconnect follow different manufacturing paths before assembly joins them. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Logic die
nodes.detail: The foundry builds the processor circuit.

nodes.label: Memory stacks
nodes.detail: Memory manufacturers build and test DRAM dies.

nodes.label: Interposer and substrate
nodes.detail: Separate manufacturing creates the connections.

nodes.label: Accelerator package
nodes.detail: Assembly joins these streams into one system.

title: Who enables a chip designer?
caption: A fabless designer depends on several specialist capabilities; no single purchasing relationship explains the whole chain. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: EDA and IP
nodes.detail: Tools and reusable blocks help define the circuit.

nodes.label: Foundry
nodes.detail: The manufacturing process turns a layout into devices.

nodes.label: Assembly and test
nodes.detail: Partners connect dies and screen finished parts.

nodes.label: Fabless product
nodes.detail: The designer coordinates the resulting chip product.

title: Capacity depends on complementary capabilities
caption: The course highlights lithography, advanced packaging and HBM as interdependent constraints; these are not interchangeable capacity pools. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: EUV patterning
nodes.detail: Leading logic needs scarce patterning capability.

nodes.label: HBM supply
nodes.detail: Memory dies must also be manufactured and stacked.

nodes.label: Advanced assembly
nodes.detail: Logic and memory need dense package connections.

nodes.label: Shippable accelerator
nodes.detail: All required inputs must arrive and pass their checks.

title: The fab loop inside the longer journey
caption: Deposition, patterning, removal and measurement recur many times before a wafer is complete; this cycle is nested inside the sand-to-rack flow. Schematic, not to scale.
